title: The Nasdaq's Worst Week Since 2020. Now What?
description:
The Nasdaq Composite fell 10.0% in the week to Nov 20, 2026, its worst week since March 2020. The S&P 500 fell 8.6%, its worst week since April 2025, and closed at 6,910.39: 11.6% below its Oct 6 record, which makes it a correction. We go through the week day by day, why stocks fell (bond yields over 5%, 4.1% inflation, the Fed's September hike, the tech unwind, a fear index at 37), where the money went (gold -9.5%, bitcoin -13.8%, Treasuries up), and every S&P 500 correction since 1950: 26 of them, 15 stopped before a bear market, and a year after first hitting -10% the index was higher 18 of 26 times (median +14%).

FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis): DGS10, DFEDTARU/DFEDTARL, CPIAUCSL, MORTGAGE30US (Freddie Mac). Correction statistics are our calculations from S&P 500 closes since 1950, prices only (no dividends): a correction is a close 10% or more below the prior record, finished at the next record.
